project: Rare Disease, Real Kid: The MVA Hackathon 2026

data_access_granted.how: Automatic: python tools/check_access.py each run. The user requests access personally on the dataset page (it is their attestation to the data-use terms).

llm_terms_confirmed.record: Anthropic Claude Max (consumer plan), used through Claude Code; model-training opt-out enabled ('Help improve Claude' off); no feedback or ratings given in sessions involving the data. This meets Sage's conditions for consumer plans (HF thread #2, 2026-09-29). Confirmed by Santanu in a live chat on 2026-09-30.
llm_terms_confirmed.how: The user names their Claude plan and verifies its data-handling terms in a live chat (HF thread #21: a consumer plan with training off is not enough on its own; commercial/API terms are recommended). The confirmed wording goes in 'record' and into both methods reports.

setup_downloads_done.record: Installed 2026-09-30 (tools/setup_core.sh; log D:\mva-hackathon\logs\r08_setup_core.log). bcftools, samtools and htslib 1.24 and minimap2 2.31-r1302, in a micromamba env under D:\mva-hackathon\tools (780 MB after cleaning the package cache). GRCh38 no-alt analysis set with hs38d1, 2,580 contigs renamed without chr (1..22, X, Y, M), faidx-indexed (3.0 GB). ClinVar GRCh38 VCF, fileDate 2026-09-28 (190 MB). Ensembl GRCh38 GFF3 release 116 (104 MB). Organisers' templates. About 1.3 GB downloaded; about 4.1 GB on disk.
setup_downloads_done.how: Approved in a live chat on 2026-09-30 (laptop, VCF-first route): the ~1.5 GB core set, all under D:\mva-hackathon, deleted after the competition. It covers a micromamba env with bcftools, samtools, htslib and minimap2 in D:\mva-hackathon\tools; the GRCh38 no-alt analysis set with hs38d1 (contigs renamed without chr), the Ensembl GRCh38 GFF3 and the ClinVar GRCh38 VCF in refs; and the organisers' templates (fetched 2026-09-30). True once installed and checked (package R08).

hf_space_route.how: Chosen, then dropped the same day: Hugging Face returned 402, because hosting Docker/Gradio Spaces on free cpu-basic needs a PRO subscription. Santanu then chose the laptop, VCF-first route (live chat). The CLAUDE.md exception for private HF compute and the code in space/ stay in case he subscribes. Kaggle stays public-data only.

hf_space_token_set.how: Only needed if the HF Space route is revived: Santanu would create a fine-grained, read-only HF token and paste it himself as the secret HF_TOKEN. Claude never handles the token.

dataset_downloaded.how: Approved in a live chat on 2026-09-30 (laptop, VCF-first route). Once access is granted, download the VCF, its index and the phenotype document to D:\mva-hackathon\data and verify checksums against the HF metadata. FASTQ pairs are fetched one pair at a time for overnight low-priority jobs and deleted after use. True once the VCF, index and phenotype document are in place (package D00).

github_repo_created.how: Live session: the user approves a PRIVATE repo under SanTanBan. It must be made public after the hackathon, again with a live yes.

nightly_push_enabled.how: Only if the user explicitly opts in: push code-only commits to the private repo at the end of each run.

track1.policy: Stage once early to bank the score, then only when the report materially improves.

track2.policy: Only the LATEST is judged. Stage the final version only, by 2026-10-23.

packages.title: Request dataset access on Hugging Face
packages.done_when: check_access.py reports dataset_access = granted. Critical path: nothing counts without it, and registration IS this request.

packages.title: Confirm Claude plan and its data-handling terms
packages.done_when: gates.llm_terms_confirmed is true with a recorded one-line disclosure.

packages.title: Track 1 CSV validator
packages.done_when: Enforces the published field spec, including the chr prefix; tested on synthetic rows.

packages.title: Track 2 scientific core: report draft v1
packages.done_when: Covers the mechanism of BUBR1 insufficiency (dosage, pseudokinase, acetylation/degradation); the landscape check (ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN incl. MILI, ChEMBL, Open Targets including the two tractability traps); ranked candidates, each with evidence and its honest problem; the do-not-use list (MPS1/TTK, Aurora B, PLK1, pan-HDAC at high dose, growth hormone); the six-point chemo-compatibility screen; the five-assay decision rule with the mitotic-duration veto; KIF18A and the oligonucleotide lane; limitations. Each claim is cited by PMID or DOI and spot-checked in PubMed. Fix the known memo errors: CEP57 is Snape et al. 2011, and there is no unsourced penetrance figure.

packages.title: BUB1B locus dossier from public data
packages.done_when: Covers the MANE Select transcript and exon/domain map; known P/LP variants cited by ClinVar ID and HGVS (no raw coordinates); the upstream regulatory interval and the deep-intronic/mobile-element precedents; the BUB1 paralog mapping caveat; Genomics England PanelApp panels; gnomAD constraint; the other MVA genes to exclude. Public data only.

packages.progress: 2026-09-27: renderer (public/full split, Markdown + PDF via headless Edge, 10 tests) and a provisional skeleton. 2026-09-30: the organisers' form (methods_description_form.xlsx, one sheet per track, in D:\mva-hackathon\refs\templates) was fetched from their Space. reports/track1/methods_report.md now answers its 13 Track 1 questions as Part A, and reports/track2/methods_description.md answers the 11 Track 2 questions. The required acknowledgement is added to both reports and the pitch.
packages.title: Report scaffolds with public and submitted variants
packages.done_when: The Track 1 methods report skeleton follows the organizers' methods template sections, including the LLM-usage question. A renderer produces a redacted public version into reports/ and a full version into D:\mva-hackathon\submissions, as Markdown and PDF.

packages.progress: All seven components have scripts and synthetic tests (20 pass). End-to-end runs need the U3 toolchain and reference (minimap2, bcftools, GRCh38).
packages.title: Analysis code, tested on synthetic data
packages.done_when: Scripts, each with a tiny synthetic test: VCF QC and normalisation (no-chr contigs, add chr on output); rare-recessive filter and compound-het pairing; per-chromosome B-allele-fraction mosaicism from VCF AD; low-pass depth from head-of-FASTQ alignment; BUB1B locus k-mer baiting; ACMG SF v3.3 screen; ACMG points calculator. Designed for 4 threads and 7.8 GB RAM with nothing large on C:.

packages.progress: pipeline/drug_triage (sources, flags, triage, panel.json), 10 offline tests; demo in reports/track2/drug_triage/. API cache at D:\mva-hackathon\refs\drug_triage_cache; rerun with --offline. 2026-09-29: CYP3A4 flag fixed for weak and time-dependent perpetrators (givinostat, dasatinib); demo regenerated, tier counts unchanged.
packages.title: Scalable drug-triage pipeline (public data only)
packages.done_when: Given a set of checkpoint genes, it pulls public data (ChEMBL, Open Targets, openFDA labels) and flags paediatric approval, checkpoint-weakening mechanism, aneugen class, CYP3A4 interaction, nephrotoxicity and myelosuppression, then outputs a ranked table. Demo on BUB1B, TRIP13 and CEP57. This is the Scalability argument.

packages.progress: About 370 spoken words (2:40 at 140 wpm), 7 slides, opens with the veto rule. 2026-09-29: five registries, the German adolescent metformin trial and a rules-fixed-in-advance line added. Refresh slide 4 after D08.
packages.title: Pitch script and slide outline (3 minutes)
packages.done_when: Timed to 3:00 or less and opens with the veto rule, not a biology lecture.

packages.title: Public BUB1B splice map on Kaggle (Pangolin, every possible SNV)
packages.done_when: A private Kaggle notebook scores every possible SNV across the BUB1B gene with Pangolin (GPL-3.0). Positive controls behave as expected: canonical splice variants lose, and c.2386-11A>G gains. Results (a few MB) are in D:\mva-hackathon\refs\bub1b. The worksheet gains a summary of where antisense-correctable cryptic sites could arise. No patient data is involved.

notes: 2026-09-27: First routine run. Access still not granted (HTTP 403). Done: R02 Track 2 report v1 (69 PubMed-checked citations; landscape re-run), R03 locus dossier (classic hypomorphic alleles are VUS or conflicting in ClinVar; BUB1 paralog shares no 21-mer with BUB1B coding sequence; PanelApp cataract panel is red), R05 pipeline (20 tests). R04 partial. Nothing staged.

2026-09-27 (second run, evening): Access still 403. Done: R06 drug-triage pipeline (Open Targets + ChEMBL + openFDA; 133 rows over BUB1B/TRIP13/CEP57; all 28 TTK/AURKB/PLK1 controls and 11/12 HDAC2/3 candidates excluded automatically; 30 tests pass) and R07 pitch script. R04 still waits on the organisers' methods template (U3). Every remaining routine package is now blocked on U1/U2/U3/U5. Nothing staged.

2026-09-29: Access still 403 (25.6 days left). No package was runnable, so did public-data v2 prep on done work. Track 2 report is now v1.1: EU CTIS, ANZCTR and WHO ICTRP searched (no MVA trials; found a German adolescent+adult metformin prevention trial in Li-Fraumeni, CTIS 2025-520714-63-00, added to H3); the section 6 screen is filled from hand-read US labels and 6 new PubMed-checked sources; H2 x H3 OCT2 interaction noted; givinostat thrombocytopenia corrected to the label figure (33% vs 0%); benzimidazole evidence added to section 5; Ensembl NMD isoforms of BUB1B listed in section 8.1 (exon 5 skip most recurrent). R06 CYP3A4 flag bug fixed (52 tests pass). Local pytest needs PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 because a third-party plugin wants the missing zstandard module. Nothing staged.

2026-09-29 (second run, evening): Access still 403 (25.4 days left). No package runnable. D08 prep: allele-mechanism and antisense rules pre-registered before data access (worksheet + pipeline/allele_mechanism.py, 18 tests; 70 pass in total). Finding: no BUB1B exon is likely eligible for skipping; exon 17 is the best in-frame candidate but carries the destabilising MVA substitution R727C, so realistic antisense routes are splice correction and up-regulation. Track 2 report v1.2: VAEAOT is the N1C VARIANT guidelines (Cheerie 2025a, PMID 40139194); Suijkerbuijk 2010 threshold (6% vs 13% BUBR1) and HSP90-dependence of kinase-domain mutants added. Pitch refreshed (~370 words). Ensembl REST returned 500/503, so NCBI RefSeq NM_001211.6 was used (saved to D:\mva-hackathon\refs\bub1b). Nothing staged.
